task.title: Bring zero-foreground-latency craft guidance to Conversation mode
task.source: User request for Narrative-Craft-level solo and group Conversation quality without setup or added reply latency
task.classification: engine prompt policy, detached Agent analysis, cadence, memory, and background scheduling

coreClaim: Every solo and group Conversation writer receives a compact first-reply craft guide in its existing provider call; when Agents are enabled, a configured-model critic analyzes saved replies after visible completion and stores one validated correction for a later reply without competing with foreground generation.
rootCause: Conversation mode had strong general texting rules but no final compact anti-assistant guide, no evidence-gated adaptive critic, and no shared detached lifecycle across ordinary, group-child, and direct-message generation.

inScope: First-reply solo and group Conversation guidance
Automatic hidden craft critic with a Conversation-specific prompt
Configured default Agent connection and model resolution
First eligible reply then four-assistant-message cadence
Exact assistant-evidence validation and deterministic directives
Shared latest-job-wins craft queue and foreground cancellation
Normal, group-child, direct-message, preview, and dry-run prompt parity
outOfScope: A synchronous rewrite or second foreground provider call
A universal guarantee for every stochastic provider sample
StoryScope as a release oracle for casual texting
A new setting, schema, UI, or required user action
Changing the configured writer or Agent model

claimBoundary.coreClaim: The writer receives one final advisory block inside its existing request; only exact excerpts from assistant messages can select one engine-owned next-turn directive, and new foreground generation cancels pending or running craft analysis.
claimBoundary.riskType: prompt, provider, persistence, cadence, async ordering, and cross-entrypoint compatibility
entrypoints: Sequential or selected group child generation
currentPathsOrFormats: narrative-craft runtime with Conversation-specific prompt and gate
legacyPathsOrFormats: Existing Conversation chats with no craft Agent active ID
outOfScopeClaims: No claim that every reply will be preferred by every reader.
No claim that detached analysis has zero token or quota cost.
No claim that StoryScope's fiction classifier measures conversational naturalness.
No claim that sampled provider wall-clock timing predicts future latency.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: Conversation quality guidance was diffuse and static, while Narrative Craft's evidence-gated adaptive loop was roleplay-only.
contractLaneGate.producer: The Conversation writer produces and saves an assistant message.
contractLaneGate.consumer: The final writer guide and the next eligible Conversation prompt consume baseline or one-shot guidance.
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: Quality guidance must apply from the first reply, use the configured Agent model for later analysis, remain grounded in written assistant text, and stay outside foreground latency.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: The generation guide owns the first-reply baseline; agent-runner reuses Narrative Craft's configured-model resolution and cadence; the executor selects the Conversation evidence gate; shared agent memory owns one-shot state; the scheduler owns detachment, coalescing, and foreground cancellation.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The engine owns prompt construction, provider resolution, generated output, persistence, and background lifecycle.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not rewrite visible text in React, add a synchronous critic call, trust model-authored directives, mutate chat activation metadata, or use StoryScope to score texting.
regressionProof: Focused prompt tests prove one final Conversation Craft wrapper in solo and group modes and none outside Conversation.
Executor tests reject invented evidence, group-only issues in solo, and arbitrary model-authored advice.
Runtime tests prove automatic activation, configured provider resolution, four-message cadence, Agent-disabled behavior, replay preservation, and direct-run isolation.
Lifecycle tests prove visible done precedes the critic for normal, direct, and group generation, while shared queue tests prove coalescing and cancellation.

positiveRows.claim: The final Conversation Craft wording directionally improves the measured Conversation-quality gate.
positiveRows.evidence: Across 10 paired GLM writer cases and 21 usable randomized blind judgments, treatment won 13, baseline won 7, and 1 tied; solo was 8-4 and group was 5-3-1.

positiveRows.claim: The critic adds no foreground provider round trip.
positiveRows.evidence: Runtime construction makes zero provider requests; normal, direct, and group lifecycle tests reach done after writer calls and before the critic starts.

positiveRows.claim: Group behavior improves without forcing a universal omnireply.
positiveRows.evidence: The final blind group subset favored treatment 5-3-1; the guide preserves relevant open questions while rejecting other participants' direct mentions and allowing silence or a minimal reaction.

contradictionRows.claim: Model-produced instructions must not enter the next prompt.
contradictionRows.evidence: The hostile-output test supplies a prompt-injection string as model text and proves the executor replaces it with the engine-owned directive selected by grounded issue code.

contradictionRows.claim: A solo conversation must not accept group-only diagnoses.
contradictionRows.evidence: The executor rejects group-omnireply in solo mode, while group-voice-collapse requires two distinct exact assistant excerpts.

contradictionRows.claim: A new foreground request must not wait for prior analysis.
contradictionRows.evidence: The shared scheduler aborts running analyses and discards pending jobs across chats when a foreground lease begins.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Existing Conversation chats receive the feature without metadata migration or setup.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Automatic runtime tests begin with activeAgentIds empty and still resolve Conversation Craft; the engine never writes the active ID to chat metadata.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Agents-disabled chats keep baseline quality but spend no adaptive Agent call.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: The lifecycle test sees the Conversation Craft writer guide and exactly one writer request, then proves no critic starts.

untestedRows: Spark produced malformed JSON for 9 of 10 final judge requests after three attempts; all failures are retained in the scratch artifact and excluded rather than silently repaired.
The final live evaluation is a 10-pair synthetic sample, not a production confidence interval or guarantee for every model and character.
No StoryScope score is claimed because its fiction-trained dimensions are not a valid oracle for casual chat replies.

ownedFacts.description: Conversation Craft uses its configured connection and model, then the default Agent connection, then the current writer connection.
ownedFacts.evidence: Agent resolution tests and existing connection fallback tests exercise the shared agent-runner path; no Conversation-specific provider bypass exists.

ownedFacts.description: Only one validated directive can be pending and it is consumed once.
ownedFacts.evidence: The shared craft memory normalizer bounds pendingGuidance to one item and runtime tests consume it once while preserving diagnostic state.

ownedFacts.description: The final live sample did not show added writer latency.
ownedFacts.evidence: Mean provider wall clock was 3277 ms for treatment and 4435 ms for the reused baseline, but this is reported only as a noisy sample; deterministic tests own the one-call latency claim.

manualBlockers.reason: GLM and Terra completed all 20 required judgments, Spark completed one, and every unavailable result is recorded; no writer model judged its own output alone.

reviewThreadLedger.finding: The first evaluation wording could over-compress caring replies and ignore relevant group-open questions.
reviewThreadLedger.fix: The final guide says brevity is not itself a goal, preserves character-appropriate care and useful specifics, keeps relevant open questions, and explicitly permits silence when nothing belongs to the character.

verification.baselineCommand: pnpm vitest run <Conversation Craft focused suites> && pnpm typecheck
verification.baselineEvidence: The final combined focused suite passed 99 tests; full repository verification runs in the release gate.
edgeRowsTested: First eligible and fourth assistant cadence
negativeRowsTested: No critic when Agents are disabled
